mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or if the mechanism fails during a high-inflation shock.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or if GDP growth recovers while the signal fires.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months, combined with accelerating average hourly earnings growth (implied by PAYEMS and UNRATE dynamics), signals a tight labor market that boosts wage inflation and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or if inflation does not accelerate as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, reducing corporate revenue prospects and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or if the decline is reversed within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% while the federal funds rate remains above 4% signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which increases real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or if inflation rebounds above 3% within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or if the retail sales momentum breaks within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.3% in the same month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change > 0.3% AND PAYEMS monthly change < -0.3%
failure_condition: If S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or if the labor market recovers within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals insufficient demand to sustain earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or if GDP growth accelerates above 2% within the next quarter.
